Senses.Explanation: The numeral "one" (一) plus "thing" or "object" (物): "one thing," attested 2,625 times in 353 allowlisted texts. Its Chan deployment includes positive, negative, indefinite, and deliberately unnamed forms. In the Nanyue-Huineng encounter, Nanyue says that "to describe it as one thing would not hit it" (說似一物即不中), after eight years of inquiry. Huineng's verse says, "awakening originally has no tree; the bright mirror is not a stand; originally there is not one thing; where could dust alight?" (菩提本無樹，明鏡亦非臺，本來無一物，何處惹塵埃). A lamp question quotes, "the hundred bones all collapse and scatter; one thing remains constantly numinous—what is the one thing?" and receives "what suffering, buddha!" (百骸俱潰散，一物鎮長靈；如何是一物；苦哉佛陀耶). Another address says, "outside, not one thing can establish [anything]; all are the original mind producing ten thousand kinds of things" (外無一物而能建立，皆是本心生萬種法). Later speakers also challenge anyone "not relying on one thing" (不依倚一物). These records use the ordinary noun precisely: sometimes an unnamed referent is proposed, sometimes even that label is rejected, and sometimes the phrase negates every external thing.
Senses.Note: Counted constructions: "originally not one thing" (本來無一物), 214; "to describe it as one thing would not hit it" (說似一物即不中), 105; "there is one thing" (有一物), 385; "not one thing" (無一物), 918; "not rely on one thing" (不依倚一物), 69. These contrasting constructions do not justify turning "one thing" into a fixed metaphysical entity.

Occurrences.Kwic: 說似一物即不中祖云還假修證也無
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), Nanyue Huairang's biography. After eight years attending Huineng, Nanyue Huairang reports his insight by saying that describing it as one thing would miss it; Huineng then asks whether cultivation and verification are still needed. Huineng is the respondent, not the speaker of the headword-bearing statement.

Occurrences.Kwic: 百骸俱潰散一物鎮長靈。如何是一物。師曰。苦哉佛陀耶。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continued Transmission of the Lamp (續傳燈錄), Fengqi Zhongqing entry. An unnamed monk is the exact questioner who asks what the one thing is; all six attribution rungs, including parallel occurrences of the formula and the unique full exchange, leave this questioner unnamed. Fengqi Zhongqing gives the following answer, while Xuedou Chongxian is only the lineage-header teacher.
